newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tyndall says trading ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tyndall says trading ahead of budget.

text.p: Financial services group Tyndall Australid Ltd said on Wednesday it was trading ahead of budget expectations for the year to date and was confident that the outlook for calendar 1997 was encouraging.

"The company remains in a healthy financial position. on the basis of the year to date results, we are trading ahead of budget expectations and remain confident that the outlook for the full year ahead is encouraging. This, however, is dependent on the vagaries of investment markets," said Tyndall chairman Peter Cary.
Tyndall's net profit for calendar 1996 rose 29.2 percent to A$22.07 million.
Tyndall said during calendar 1997 it planned to integrate fully the operations of the Oceanic group of companies which it bought in January this year for A$40.5 million.
"This is at some cost in terms of time and effort. I am pleased to say that, today, it is proceeding well," the chairman said.
Cary said the Oceanic group complemented the company's current risk insurance operations as well as bringing about A$200 million in new funds to the group.
He said in 1997 the company would again be looking for opportunities to grow its business.

"Thus far this year we have conducted an unsuccessful due diligence on one opportunity and have recently completed a transaction to acquire the New Zealand-based investment management business of BZW Investment Management," Cary said.
He said the 1997 year would see the company continue its concentration on developing its core business activities in order to become a focused financial services group in the trans-Tasman arena.
Tyndall's shares were untraded by 11.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), after having closed up five cents at A$2.00 on Tuesday.
Tyndall is 52 percent owned by Sir Ron Brierley's Guinness Peat Group Plc.
